reports.title: Post Holdings Reports Results for the Fourth Quarter and Fiscal Year 2026

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: Post management expects Adjusted EBITDA for fiscal year 2027 to be between $1,450-$1,500 million. Post management expects fiscal year 2027 capital expenditures to range between $360-$400 million, which includes continued Foodservice investment in cage-free egg facility expansion and Post Consumer Brands investment in nut butter manufacturing optimization.

desk.headline: Sales down 13% to $1.95bn, below estimates; adjusted EPS $1.84 beats; FY27 adjusted EBITDA guided to $1.45-1.50bn, below FY26
results: Q4 sales fell 13% to $1.95bn; $138.5m of last year's sales came from businesses since sold, and egg prices lapped last year's bird-flu spike.
Pet food volumes fell 12.7% and cereal and granola 4.4%, on distribution losses and shrinking categories.
Foodservice segment profit fell 29% as egg pricing normalised, while Post Consumer Brands profit rose 46%.
Adjusted EPS was $1.84 (down from $2.20) but beat estimates; GAAP EPS rose to $1.68 as last year had a goodwill write-down.
For the full year, Post bought back $1.01bn of shares (10.3m) and generated $563m of free cash flow.

guidance.summary: Post expects fiscal 2027 adjusted EBITDA of $1.45-1.50bn, below the $1.57bn just reported, and capital spending of $360-400m. In August management had pointed to a comparable base of about $1.48bn for FY27, so the range sits around that level.

Leadership: Executive Chairman Rob Vitale is on medical leave; CEO Nicolas Catoggio leads the company.
